{{nihongo|'''Ikuhime Shrine'''|伊久比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

[[ja:伊久比売神社]]

'''Ikuhime Shrine''' (いくひめじんじゃ) is a shrine in Ichishōji, {{ill|Wakayama (city)|Q200747|qid=Q200747}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=candidate Shikinaisha}} identified with "Ikuhime Shrine" in Nagusa District, {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053}}, in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'. Today it is revered as {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} of Jirōmaru and Nobutoki in Kishi district, and of Kusumi and Nozaki districts in Wakayama City<ref>'Wakayamashi Yō' (revised 5th ed.), Wakayama City, 1965.</ref>. Former {{ill|Q712534|lt=village shrine}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*'''Ikuhime-no-Mikoto'''
The '{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}' infers from the shrine location name "Ichishōji" and local calling of the deity as "Ichihime Daimyōjin" that a {{ill|Marketplace|Q330284|qid=Q330284}} existed here before early modern times and "Ichihime" was enshrined as its guardian. The current deity is taken as Ikuhime-no-Mikoto, but there are other theories<ref>{{ill|Tōgo Yoshida|Q11413910|qid=Q11413910}}'s '{{ill|Dai Nippon Chimei Jisho|Q17213149|qid=Q17213149}}' argues "I'''ku'''hime" may be an error for "I'''ya'''hime," paired with Iyato deity of {{ill|Iyato Shrine|Q11458562|qid=Q11458562}} in Muatani, that Iyato deity is Ōyabiko-no-Kami (another name of {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Kami}}), and thus Iya-hime may be {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōyatsuhime}}. Also, {{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|qid=Q108780926}}'s '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|ja|神名帳考証|qid=Q11588824}}' (completed 1733) and '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nanki Jinja-roku}}' (published 1746) identify the deity as {{ill|Wakahiru-me|ja|稚日女尊|zh|稚日女尊|qid=Q11596349}}.</ref>.

=== Origin ===
Founding origin is unknown, but a tradition says that in {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|de|Tempyō-Hōji|es|Tenpyō-hōji|fa|تنپیو-هوجی|fr|Ère Tenpyō-hōji|ia|Tenpyo-hoji|id|Tempyō-hōji|ja|天平宝字|ko|덴표호지|ru|Тэмпё-ходзи|simple|Tenpyō-hōji|sr|Тенпјо хоџи|tr|Tenpyō-hōji|uk|Темпьо-Ходзі (ненґо)|zh|天平宝字|zh_yue|天平寶字|qid=Q1346307}} 8 (764), when foreign enemies attacked, a person named Fujiwara Sadakuni was appointed general to subdue them, and after victorious return he received divine revelation and offered sacred gifts<ref>'{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kii Meisho Zue}}'.</ref>. If so, the shrine existed before the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}.

By shrine tradition, it is the "Ikuhime Shrine" of the Engishiki list and the "Senior Fourth Upper Ikuhime deity" among 30 earthly deities in Nagusa District of the '{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|ja|紀伊国神名帳|qid=Q17210008}}'. However, '{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}' states that because this lower {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kinokawa}} area was repeatedly flooded and later saw warfare, origins are unclear. From its old name "Ichihime Daimyōjin" and local place name Ichishōji, it reasons that a market opened in this area before the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, and this shrine was invited as its {{ill|Guardian deities|ja|守護神|qid=Q131278957}} after villages formed as the coastline retreated. After {{ill|Tokugawa Yorinobu|eo|Tokugawa Yorinobu|es|Tokugawa Yorinobu|fa|توکوگاوا یورینوبو|fr|Tokugawa Yorinobu|ja|徳川頼宣|ko|도쿠가와 요리노부|pt|Tokugawa Yorinobu|ru|Токугава Ёринобу|uk|Токугава Йорінобу|zh|德川賴宣|qid=Q1045763}} entered Kii, old traces were examined and this shrine was identified and renamed; then in {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 11 (1726), precinct boundaries were set and it came to appear as an ancient shrine, becoming ubusunagami of four villages in Kusumi-shō<ref>Not a shōen estate but an early-modern settlement unit derived from the ancient/medieval Kusumi-gō.</ref> (Jirōmaru, Ichishōji, Naka-no, Funadoko<ref>Corresponding to present-day Oaza Jirōmaru, Ichishōji, Kusumi-naka, and Funadoko.</ref>)<ref>'Kii Zoku Fudoki.' According to 'Kusumi-shō Ikuhime Shrine Saikenza-chō' (in 'Wakayamashi-shi' vol.6), an order recognizing it as Shikinaisha was issued June 28, Kyōhō 11, and by Feb 3 of the next year a notice board was erected stating Shikinaisha status and "no killing" in precinct.</ref>.

=== Engishiki "Ikuhime Shrine" ===
The Engishiki shrine's whereabouts were already unknown before early modern times. As above, this shrine came to be identified after Yorinobu entered Kii, but '{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}' was skeptical, saying this land was under sea before Engishiki and "the site shape is not that of a great shrine," suggesting that even if this were the Engishiki shrine, it may have been moved from a site to the northeast. In contrast, physical geography confirms Kinokawa channel changes but shows this site was not under sea or river channel in the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, so a local ubusunagami-type shrine may have long stood at current location<ref name="角川地名">'Kadokawa Nihon Chimei Daijiten.'</ref><ref name="平凡社地名">'Place Names of Wakayama Prefecture.'</ref>. As this area was an inlet coast in antiquity<ref name="平凡社地名"/> and later had Kii port with an adjacent market through medieval times, a shrine to "Ichihime" as market guardian may have been founded<ref name="角川地名"/><ref name="平凡社地名"/>. Even in that case, it does not necessarily mean that shrine was Engishiki-listed, and since identification occurred only from Edo onward, substantial room for re-examination remains<ref name="角川地名"/><ref name="平凡社地名"/>.

=== Ritual organization ===
In early modern times, a {{ill|miyaza|ja|宮座|qid=Q11454763}} of four villages (Jirōmaru, Ichishōji, Naka-no, Funadoko) is said to have held hereditary rights to participate in shrine rites<ref>'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku.' In the above Saikenza-chō, 17 members are known: 3 from Naka-no, 7 from Ichishōji, 4 from Funadoko, 3 from Jirōmaru.</ref>, though details are now unclear<ref>'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku.'</ref>. Soon after domain recognition as Shikinaisha, in June Kyōhō 13, Tanaka Tōbei of Ichishōji village in the miyaza was appointed {{ill|Kannushi (disambiguation)|ja|神主|ko|신주|zh|神主|qid=Q15888735}} as "person of proper lineage" by the domain<ref>Above Saikenza-chō.</ref>.

Current annual festival day is October 13.

=== Shrine buildings ===
The honden is {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684|lt=ikken-sha nagare-zukuri}} with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=copper-plate roof}} and has {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234}}. The haiden is a tiled {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=wari-haiden}}.

=== Massha ===
Sato-gami Shrine<ref>Former unranked shrine in Funadoko.</ref>, Hachiman-sha and Hachioji-sha (one building, {{ill|Aidono|Q135009883|qid=Q135009883}})<ref>Former unranked shrine in Ichishōji Aza Gongen, relocated in Meiji 43.</ref>, Sumiyoshi Shrine<ref>Former unranked shrine in Kusumi-naka Aza Danzuka, relocated in Meiji 41.</ref>, Konpira-gū<ref>Former unranked shrine in Hirai.</ref>, Kusumoto Hakuryū Ōkami, Myōken-sha, Hachiman-sha, Hachiman Shrine, Kuzu Shrine<ref>Former unranked shrine in Awa.</ref>, Kasuga Shrine, and a small stone pagoda carved with "Ujisha Ryō Daimyōjin / Amaterasu Kōtai Jingū, Konpira Daigongen." Most were relocated at the end of Meiji as noted above.
